narrative: Your application was denied because the model estimated a 77% chance you would fail the bar exam on your first attempt, which the admissions process treated as too high a risk to admit. The strongest driver was your third-year class rank: you were in the lowest decile, while admitted students averaged around the sixth decile. That low rank pushed the prediction strongly toward failure. Your first-year class rank was the second most important factor, and it pointed the same way: you were also in the lowest decile, compared with an admitted-student average near the sixth decile. Your undergraduate GPA was the third most important factor. At 2.10 it is below the admitted-student average of 3.23, but in the model’s overall assessment this factor leaned slightly toward passing rather than failing. Even so, the two low class-rank signals outweighed it and drove the denial. To strengthen a future application, focus on creating clear evidence that you can handle rigorous law-school work and pass the bar. Ask admissions for feedback, retake the LSAT if you can improve it, consider additional coursework or a post-baccalaureate record that raises your academic profile, and apply to a broader set of schools with a plan to demonstrate improved readiness.
